cohort: The study participants are women from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1979 in the United States.
finding: Women with birth intervals longer than two years but no longer than six years had the smallest penalties for cumulative outcomes, but postponement of a first birth to at least age 30 appeared to be more important for cumulative outcomes than birth spacing.
followup_time: Until midlife (approximately 46-53 years of age for the cohort by 2010)
